visual_checks.evidence: Diff PNG shows scattered low-magnitude per-pixel deltas (expected from bf16 round-off propagating through exp), but no structural diff patterns — no seams, no halos, no localized failure modes.

reasoning: Kernel 26.321 → 25.442 ms (-3.34%) — a real win. PSNR drops slightly (-0.27 dB hero, -0.03 side, -0.26 top) but all views comfortably above 35 dB floor. The change drops the defensive `min(power, 0)` clamp before exp_tile<true>. For valid PSD covariance, Q ≥ 0 mathematically so -0.5·Q ≤ 0 by construction. bf16 round-off can produce tiny positive `power` (~ε), but exp_tile<true>'s built-in ClampToNegative and the downstream 0.99 alpha cap bound any deviation. Distinct from iter-046's regression: iter-046 REPLACED the clamp with clamp_tile + clamp_tile_init (a different op shape that was internally slower); this iter simply REMOVES the chain. The explicit `exp_tile_init<true>()` after `mul_unary_tile` resets SFPU state directly, so removing binary_min_tile_init() before it doesn't disrupt exp init — unlike iter-046's hypothesized state dependency. Saved 4 SFPU ops/Gaussian. Visual: 3 views look clean and identical to reference, diff10 shows low-magnitude scattered pixel deltas with no structural patterns. KEEP.
